03 · Two ways to play

Choose at New Game

Histoire · Story

  • 62 quests in four lanes, each opening the next
  • Four great deeds, then the descent into the Heart
  • A painted page in the My Story book for every quest
  • Ends with a lullaby and the credits; the world carries on

Survie · Survival

  • The endless game: score = hours survived
  • Rewards unlock with days and milestones instead of quests
  • Nights grow harder, up to 14 attackers
  • A lost day after a collapse never counts

Both modes: same world, gentle mode for young players, maths level 1–6 changeable at any time.

Play

Open the file and go

No install and no account. The game runs in Chrome on a computer or a phone held sideways.

  1. Open mine-moule.html

    Download it from the repository and open it in your browser. On a phone, turn it sideways.

  2. Start a New Game

    Pick a name, a world, a season length, Story or Survival, and a maths level from 1 to 6.

  3. Build the bed first

    Gather wood and webs, craft at the workbench, and be inside before the first night.

  4. Keep your save safe

    Saves live in the browser. Export one from the pause menu; import it from the title screen.

Design

The decisions behind the game

The main choices we made, grouped by topic, each with the reason behind it.

Goal and modes

  • Two modes at New Game

    Story has 62 quests and an ending; Survival is endless and scored in hours survived.

    Why One game for children who want a story and players who want a challenge.

  • Season length 7, 14 or 28 days

    Chosen at New Game; seasons change palettes, weather, food and the length of nights.

    Why Short seasons for quick games, long ones for slow builders.

  • French first, English anytime

    Every text exists in both languages; the flags switch instantly.

    Why It was made in a French-speaking home.

World

  • Generated from a seed

    Each save gets its own world: three flavours (Valley, Cove, Hills) weight the terrain types.

    Why Every new game is a new map to explore.

  • Six lands opened by the story

    The troll’s ravine leads to the Far Shore, an iron key to the North, the Frost King to the fork, four great deeds to the Heart.

    Why Progress you can see on the map.

  • Danger rings

    Monsters get tougher with distance from home and with the weeks, capped at +25 %; the far lands use fixed values.

    Why Home stays safe enough; adventure stays exciting.

Survival and home

  • Two needs: energy and hunger

    Energy empties in 2.5 days, hunger fills in 2. Food, sleep and shelter refill them.

    Why Simple enough for a child to plan around.

  • Waking up, not game over

    At zero energy you wake in your bed or shelter; in Survival that day does not count.

    Why Failure costs time, never the whole game.

  • Night sieges

    2 + day ÷ 2 attackers, up to 14, against the bed you last slept in. Two guards help after the quest “Le toit percé”.

    Why A reason to come home, without punishing long trips.

  • Villages trade or remember

    Steal freely or trade; six thefts anger a village for a season.

    Why Choices with consequences, but forgivable.

Combat

  • Full action combat

    An attack button replaces the old automatic exchange. Monsters wind up before they strike; hits knock back and give a moment of safety.

    Why Skill and timing matter; fights feel fair.

  • Blade, blunt and pierce

    Each weapon has a type, each monster a weakness worth 1.5× and armour against the rest.

    Why The bestiary becomes useful, not just a collection.

  • Gentle mode

    Halves every kind of damage, including the climates.

    Why Young players can still finish the story.

Building

  • Real but simple physics

    Blocks on a 32 px grid, up to 8 high, standing while their weight sits over a support.

    Why Easy to understand, satisfying to get right.

  • Web and metal binding

    A bound row can overhang: wood 3, stone 2, brick 4, obsidian 3, one more with metal. Web burns, so lava bridges need metal.

    Why Bridges and roofs become puzzles.

  • Shelters count as beds

    Roofed walls keep out the cold, give a respawn point and stop monsters spawning inside.

    Why Building in the wild has a purpose.

  • Spiders climb three blocks

    They try, fail and fall on taller walls. No arrow slits: walls are walls.

    Why A clear rule players can beat.

Story and learning

  • Quests are data

    The game only sends events (crafted, killed, delivered, reached); one table holds all 62 quests.

    Why Easy to add, test and balance.

  • Someone gives every quest

    Village boards, “!” villagers, Grandma’s notes in the journal, the troll and the elders.

    Why The world explains itself.

  • Maths at the player’s level

    Scholar’s stones ask grade 1–6 questions, read aloud on request; gate stones are a little harder.

    Why Practice that unlocks something real.

  • A book that writes itself

    My Story adds a painted half-page with a drop capital for every finished quest.

    Why Children see their own story grow.

Look and sound

  • 960 × 540, whole-number scaling

    32 px blocks, a hero two blocks tall, crisp on laptops and phones.

    Why Modern screens, classic pixels.

  • All art drawn by code

    Three-tone shading, 2 px outlines, dithered skies, parallax and warm night lights; monsters from sprite maps.

    Why One file, no image assets, easy to recolour.

  • Readable text first

    Nunito for every word and number, the pixel font only for the logo.

    Why The maths stones must be easy to read.

  • Twenty songs, four moods

    The Kick la Banane synth engine plays each song by day and night in four seasonal arrangements; the final lullaby is the music box tune.

    Why The music is part of the story.

Platform

  • One HTML file, no build step

    Open it in a browser and play. Chrome on desktop and phones, touch overlay, PlayStation-style pad.

    Why Nothing to install, nothing to break.

  • Saves you can carry

    Three slots in browser storage, plus export to a file and import into a free slot.

    Why Phones sometimes clear storage.

  • Tested like a product

    Playwright suites for every system and a random-input soak before each release.

    Why A family game should not crash.

The world

Six lands, one long walk

Every world is generated from a seed and saved with its slot. Each place is two to four screens of four seconds’ walk.

Homelands

27 places · start

Forests, lakes, mountains, plains, villages, cemeteries and caves around the little house. At the east end, the troll guards a ravine bridge with a maths stone.

The Far Shore

33 places · rings 1–4

Wolves, wraiths, a brigand camp, the crab beach and a hamlet. Under its lake lies the Sunken Library. An iron key opens the second crossing.

The Frozen North

12 places · cold

Fur coats, campfires and igloos keep you warm. Yetis, cursed snowmen, penguins and a grumpy walrus. The Frost King waits in the ice hall.

The Badlands

11 places · heat

A water flask, metal-bound bridges over lava, imps that burn wood and obsidian golems. The Lord of Embers guards the black forge.

The Sky Islands

10 places · wind

Wind cloaks, islands over the void, harpies and gust sprites to catch in a bottle. The Queen of Winds rules from her tower.

The Heart

5 halls · all three climates

A shaft under the house leads to the Hall of Scholars, the Hall of Climates, the Hall of the Siege and the Great Mussel.

Story mode

Grandma’s last riddle

Grandma left two things: the little house and a book of blank pages. Her notes lead through four lanes of quests to the three seals and the song that puts the Great Mussel back to sleep.

Le Foyer Home

Bed, chest, village boards, the pup, the leaking roof, the guards and forts. Ends with E1 · The Grand Siege: hold the house three nights; the guards leave you their banner.

Les Profondeurs The Depths

Caves, the miner, Grandma’s notes, the music box and the bestiary. Ends with E2 · The Sunken Library: seven stones under the lake as the water rises; the golden abacus.

Le Large The Far Shore and the North

The troll, coaches, the crab beach, the stubborn boar, the igloo elder and ice fishing. Ends with E3 · The Frost King and the first seal, the frost crown.

Les Climats The Lands

The water flask, lava bridges, the black forge, wind cloaks and the wind harps. Ends with E4 · Embers and Winds: two bosses, two seals.

The finale · Au cœur de la Mine-Moule

With all four deeds done, a shaft opens in the floor of the secret arcade room. Three harder scholar’s stones, a hall of cold, heat and wind, a siege with the village guards, and then the Great Mussel. She cannot be beaten by the sword: at half strength, play her the music box with the three seals, and she falls asleep. The credits roll, the Scholar costume unlocks, and the world carries on.

Time, needs and nights

A day lasts 5 minutes: 30 s of dawn, 180 s of day in summer (135 s in winter), 30 s of dusk, and the rest night. Seasons last 7, 14 or 28 days.

Energy empties in 2.5 days, faster when fighting, gathering or in a harsh climate without the right outfit. Hunger fills in 2 days. Raw food −25 %, cooked −40 %, bœuf bourguignon −100 %.

Sleep: a night in bed restores everything; a tent restores 75 %. At zero energy you wake in your bed or shelter.

Night sieges: 2 + day ÷ 2 attackers, up to 14. Ten seconds of bashing wears the door by a third. Two guards defend from quest F10 (Survival: day 20).

Danger rings: 0 at home to 4 at the far end of the Far Shore, plus a weekly bump capped at +25 %. The far lands use fixed values.

Build history

From a first night to the final lullaby

Each version below was playable from start to finish when it shipped. The same notes are in the game: click the version number on the title screen.

  1. 1.0.1
    • New clean, easy-to-read font for all text and numbers (the pixel font stays on the title).
    • Scholar’s stones: the question is bigger and has no shadow.
    • Fewer big boulders: about one plain in three and one mountain in two.
  2. 1.0
    • Stable release! The whole story plays from the first bed to the Great Mussel’s lullaby.
    • “!” villagers: in each village, one villager wears a “!” when a new quest is waiting. Talk to them to hear it; it goes into the journal.
    • Village guards: after “The leaking roof” (or from day 20 in Survival), two guards defend the house during sieges. With the Grand Siege banner, they also come down to the heart of the Mine-Moule.
    • Monsters no longer appear inside a shelter you built.
    • Phone: the F button moved into the margin and no longer covers window close buttons or the clock.
    • Fixes and checks across all earlier versions.
  3. 0.8
    • The Heart of the Mine-Moule: once the four great quests are done, the cellar shaft leads down to the heart.
    • Hall of Scholars: three harder scholar’s stones close the way.
    • Hall of Climates: cold, heat and wind in one hall; you need all three outfits.
    • Hall of the Siege: eight monsters from every land to beat before going on.
    • The Great Mussel: at half her life she can no longer be hurt. Play her the Scholars’ lullaby (music box + three seals) and she falls asleep.
    • End credits under the starry sky, then the world carries on. New costume: the Scholar.
    • The heart now has a real cavern backdrop: stalactites and crystals, no more sun.
  4. 0.7
    • The fork at the end of the North opens once the Frost King is beaten: the Badlands to the left, the Sky Islands to the right.
    • Badlands: heat (water flask), lava rivers to cross on a metal-bound bridge (web burns), imps that burn wood, salamanders, obsidian golems, bomb beetles, the black forge and the obsidian blade.
    • Sky Islands: wind and gusts (wind cloak, then the feathered cloak for gentle falls), islands over the void, harpies, cloud jellyfish, gargoyles at night, gust sprites to catch in a bottle (one double jump), the wind harps.
    • The Lord of Embers and the Queen of Winds guard the last two seals.
    • Each land has its own music colour, village, trades and bed.
  5. 0.6
    • The Frozen North: the second crossing (iron key + hard stone) at the end of the Far Shore leads to 12 snowy environments, an igloo village, a fishing hole and the ice hall.
    • Cold tires you: craft the fur coat (then the yeti parka), stay near a fire or in shelter. There is no cold indoors.
    • Outfit slot: one outfit at a time, chosen in the equipment panel (F).
    • Yetis, cursed snowmen (who rebuild themselves), sliding penguins, the grumpy walrus.
    • Snow blocks: dig snow, build an igloo. They melt outside the North.
    • The Frost King, the first great fight: he throws ice shards. His crown is the first seal.
    • Northern villages lend you a bed: you wake there if you fall.
  6. 0.5
    • Story mode: 62 quests in four lanes (Home, The Depths, The Far Shore, The Lands) that open one after another. Journal with J or from the pause menu.
    • My Story: the book on the bedside table writes an illustrated page for every quest you finish, with a big drop capital.
    • The troll of the Crossing guards a bridge over a ravine: answer his scholar’s stone to pass. Afterwards he trades.
    • Scholar’s stones everywhere: maths at your level (1 to 6, chosen at New Game, changeable in pause), a number pad, read-aloud for young levels. Treasure as the reward.
    • New monsters: wolf packs, wraiths at night, thief crows, charging boars, shield crabs, mimic chests, and the brigand chief’s camp with his iron key.
    • Monsters are stronger far from home and as the weeks go by (with a cap).
    • Grandma’s bestiary: a painted plate and a page for every monster you beat.
    • Village boards (deliveries, coaches), the pedlar, the pup, campfire, field bench, shell armour, silver lantern, hearty stew, gold.
    • The hamlet beyond the ravine, the sunken library and its 7 stones, and the 3-night Grand Siege.
  7. 0.4
    • Action combat: S (or ⚔ on screen, R1 on a gamepad) to strike. Monsters wind up their blows and sometimes rush you; dodge, back off, jump. Knockback and a blink after a hit.
    • The rock thrower aims and uses one stone per shot. New war hammer (metal 3, wood 1): blunt blows.
    • Weaknesses: blunt blows do 1.5× damage to skeletons, zombies and spiders; blades to brigands and goblins.
    • Gentle mode in the pause menu: monsters hurt half as much.
    • Building in the wild: bind a block with web (or metal) and it holds sideways. Roofs, ledges, bridges, towers up to 8 high.
    • New pieces: ladder, wild door, spikes, web trap. Spiders climb up to 3 high, no more.
    • Shelters: walls, a roof, your tent inside, and it is a bed. Sleep there safely and wake there if you fall.
    • The quick bar is set in the inventory (A, then 1 to 5).
    • New game: choose Story or Survival. Older games are Survival.
  8. 0.3
    • Hold ↓ for 3 seconds, standing still with no monster in sight: the hero dances to the music.
    • New animations: an axe for trees, a pickaxe for stone and ore, a hammer at the workbench and when building, bending down to pick things up, hand to mouth when eating.
    • A cracked wall left of the workbench: break it with the pickaxe to find the arcade room, with three cabinets (Kick la Banane, La Mort aux Trousses, BlocSauteur). Walk up and press E.
    • Some caves hide a secret room behind a cracked wall: a jukebox that plays every song, or a stone dragon asleep on treasure.
    • Pause: "Export save" writes your world to a file. Title screen: "Import" puts it back in a free slot. The game also asks the browser to keep its data.
  9. 0.2
    • Version number and a what’s-new log on the title screen (click the version or press V).
    • A woodpile beside every village house: 2 wood by hand. Piles refill every day in autumn, every 3 days in summer and spring, and not at all in winter.
    • One fallen log in every forest: 2 wood by hand, back after 3 days.
  10. 0.1
    • First complete playable build: title screen and three save slots, world generator with the Crossing, house with workbench, oven, bed and chest, 16 recipes and 5 dishes, energy and hunger, pickaxe harvesting, animals and fishing, five monsters, night attacks, block building with collapse physics, caves with lantern and treasure, villages with trade, and the 20-song music engine.

What comes next

Roadmap and known limits

Next

  • Costume quests: new quests that unlock hero costumes beyond the Scholar.
  • Balance from real play: tune energy, prices and monster numbers from family playtests.
  • Fonts inside the file, so the game looks the same with no internet.
  • Real-device checks on phones, tablets and a PlayStation pad.
  • Bigger saves: move to IndexedDB with compression if long games outgrow browser storage.

Known limits in 1.0.1

  • The Grand Siege is settled as door and wall damage while you sleep, not a live battle.
  • The Heart has three halls before the Mussel; a darkness stage and a collapsing climb were left out to keep the finale short for young players.
  • The village festival and guard parades are visual only.
  • Offline, the game uses a system font instead of Nunito.
  • Exporting a save needs the game opened as a file; some hosted viewers block downloads.

How it was made

Planned first

A living plan, four brainstorm rounds and a dozen review rounds checked the story, the items and the shortcuts before any code.

Built in chapters

Combat, danger, story, the North, the two lands, the finale: each chapter ended with a recorded playthrough.

Tested every time

Eleven automated suites and a random-input soak run before each release.

Made together

Idea, world and playtesting by Francis and family. Code, art, writing and music arrangements by Claude.
